newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM sees no quick end to hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM sees no quick end to hostage crisis.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto predicted on Sunday that the hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima would not be resolved quickly.
"A considerable time would be needed to resolve (the crisis)," Hashimoto told reporters. He did not elaborate.

Hashimoto made the statement hours after Peruvian President Albert Fujimori told Marxist guerrillas that a non-violent "way out" would be possible if the rebels surrendered their weapons and released their hostages.
"We think we are at a stage where we shift our demands from the safety of the hostages to the immediate release of the hostages," Hashimoto said.
"It is the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA)'s turn to respond," Hashimoto said.
Hashimoto earlier said Japan supported Fujimori's speech to the Marxist rebels holding the 340 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
